title: Dragon Siege: Post-Apocalyptic Scene Compositor
description: The user composes a post-apocalyptic siege scene where a dispersive dragon has attacked a building, leaving a damaged helmet among broken glass. Users manipulate lighting, fog density, dragon flight path, helmet placement, glass shard explosion intensity, and post-processing effects across multiple validated steps to craft a cinematic still.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load three GLB assets: GlassBrokenWindow.glb (positioned as a ruined wall facade at z=-3, scaled to fill the background), DamagedHelmet.glb (placed on the ground in front of the window at y=0, scale 1.5), and DragonDispersion.glb (hovering above and to the right at position (3,4,-1), scale 0.8). Set up a PerspectiveCamera at (0,2,8) looking at origin. Add a dark ambient light (intensity 0.15) and a movable DirectionalLight with shadows enabled. Use a dark fog (color #1a0a0a). Create an HTML control panel overlay with these validated interactions: (1) A slider for fog density (0.01-0.15) that updates scene.fog near/far, rejecting values outside range. (2) A color picker for the directional light that validates hex format and applies it. (3) A slider controlling dragon Y-axis rotation speed (0-5 rad/s) that animates the dragon orbiting the scene, with validation that speed is numeric. (4) A range slider for glass shard scatter intensity (0-2) that scales the GlassBrokenWindow model's children randomly outward from center, simulating explosion force, clamped to valid range. (5) X/Y/Z number inputs for helmet repositioning with validation that each coordinate is between -5 and 5, updating helmet position on confirm button click. (6) A dropdown to select post-processing tone mapping (NoToneMapping, ACESFilmic, Reinhard, Cineon) that updates renderer.toneMapping and validates the selection against allowed values. (7) An exposure slider (0.1-3.0) for renderer.toneMappingExposure with numeric validation. Add a ground plane with MeshStandardMaterial (dark concrete color). In the animation loop, rotate the dragon around the scene center based on the speed parameter. Display a status bar showing current parameter values. Each parameter change should log to a visible history panel showing the last 8 adjustments. Ensure all inputs validate before applying changes and show red border on invalid input.
